section_summary: This section comprises State Department records from May through July 1933 concerning internal political, economic, and diplomatic developments in Japan, centered on Tokyo Embassy Monthly Reports Nos. 78, 79, and 80 for March, April, and May 1933. The documents trace Japan's formal withdrawal from the League of Nations, military actions in Jehol and along the Great Wall, escalating friction with the Soviet Union over the Chinese Eastern Railway, and trade disputes with Great Britain and the United States. They also document internal political struggles surrounding the Saito Cabinet, the dominant role of the military, and preparations for preliminary economic discussions in Washington.

subfiles.about: Concluding portion of a chronological list of diplomatic despatches forwarded by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during February 1933.
subfiles.summary: List of despatches Nos. 285-307 sent in late February 1933, on mandated islands, Singer Sewing Machine, consular matters, treaties and the 1933 budget.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches to the Department during February 1933

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum highlighting key sections of the American Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan for March 1933.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Grew's March 1933 report: Japanese feelings toward the US, arms embargo and Soviet recognition worries, Saito Cabinet endurance, four economic laws, and record emigration to Brazil.
subfiles.title: Tokyo's Monthly Report for March, 1933

subfiles.about: Embassy despatch transmitting Report No. 78 on political, military, economic, and social conditions in Japan during March 1933.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits the Embassy's monthly report No. 78 on conditions in Japan during March 1933, accompanied by a summary, press translation, and monthly lists of Embassy telegrams and despatches. The report details Japan's formal resignation from the League of Nations, its determination to retain its South Seas mandate, military operations in Jehol and at the Great Wall, and Soviet-Japanese friction over Chinese Eastern Railway rolling stock. Domestically, it discusses the 64th Diet session, major economic control legislation, the effects of the American banking moratorium, and commercial friction involving the Ford Motor Company and Japan Steel Products Company.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 346: Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of March, 1933

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum highlighting salient points from the American Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan for April 1933.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Grew's April 1933 report: Muto's Manchurian land lease talks, Port Arthur naval base exchanges, Saito Cabinet stability, rising national debt, and dollar depreciation's effect on yen and silk.
subfiles.title: Tokyo's Monthly Report for April, 1933

subfiles.about: Embassy despatch transmitting Report No. 79 on political, diplomatic, and economic developments in Japan during April 1933.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits monthly report No. 79 covering April 1933, along with lists of Embassy despatches and telegrams and an executive summary. The report covers Japanese preparations for preliminary economic conversations in Washington led by Viscount Ishii and Eigo Fukai, ongoing fighting along the Great Wall, and Soviet-Japanese disputes concerning the Chinese Eastern Railway. It also examines British abrogation of the Indo-Japanese Trade Convention, the Dutch-Japanese arbitration treaty, the re-establishment of the Port Arthur naval base, the retention of the Saito Cabinet, and commercial difficulties encountered by Socony-Vacuum and General Electric.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 382: Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of April, 1933

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum reviewing the American Embassy's monthly report on internal political developments in Japan for May 1933.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the May 1933 political report: Takahashi stays as Finance Minister at the Genro's urging, dashing Seiyukai hopes; Araki and Ugaki reconcile; spending and taxes will rise.
subfiles.title: Tokyo's Monthly Report for May, 1933

subfiles.about: Embassy despatch transmitting Report No. 80 on political, diplomatic, and economic conditions in Japan during May 1933.
subfiles.summary: Grew sends Report No. 80 for May 1933, covering Ishii's Washington trip, tariff truce policy, Araki's Kobe speech, Admiral Taylor's visit, China, Manchukuo and the Inukai assassination report.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 419: Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of May, 1933
